facts.fact: The Danish National ID Centre note of 2 November 2023, citing the Dutch foreign ministry's report of 6 February 2017, states that a birth is first entered in the handwritten family register at the local kebabi office, which issues a transfer letter that the parents take to the sub-zoba office, where the data is entered into the database and the hard copies archived; a death goes the same way, by a 'death letter' from the kebabi to the sub-zoba.

Births and deaths are both registered in the sub-zoba's digital database after entry in the kebabi's handwritten register, according to the Dutch foreign ministry's report of 6 February 2017 as cited by the Danish National ID Centre; the note adds that there are no fixed or automatic routines for death registration.

Citing EASO (May 2015), the note states that every one of the six zobas keeps an electronic population register, first introduced in zoba Maekel in 2003, updated by the sub-zoba administrations (54 sub-zobas), while each of the approximately 2,000 kebabi administrations keeps a handwritten family register; it gives no count of offices doing the digital entry.
